# Page 5^page=5
Recall: Kronecker delta De˝nition. The Kronecker delta δij is de˝ned by δij = { 1 if i = j, 0 if i ̸= j. Properties Substitution tensor: δijaj = ai, δjiaj = ai. Dot product: a · b = δijaibj. 2 37

# Page 6^page=6
Recall: Alternating tensor De˝nition. The alternating tensor ϵijk is de˝ned by ϵijk =    0 if any of i, j, k are equal , +1 if (i, j, k) = (1, 2, 3), (2, 3, 1) or (3, 1, 2), −1 if (i, j, k) = (1, 3, 2), (2, 1, 3) or (3, 2, 1). 3 37

# Page 7^page=7
Relations of alternating tensors Relations of alternating tensors The alternating tensor ϵijk is related to The cross product of two vectors: (a × b)i = ϵijkajbk. The determinant of 3 × 3 matrices: |M | = ϵijkM1iM2jM3k, (row) |M | = ϵijkMi1Mj2Mk3. (column) The scalar triple product: a · (b × c) = ϵijkaibjck. 4 37

# Page 8^page=8
Relating δij and ϵijk Relating δij and ϵijk One can relate deltas and epsilons as follows (su˚x notation). ϵijkϵkℓm = δiℓδjm − δimδjℓ. 5 37

# Page 9^page=9
Suffix notation and ranks Intuition: What is the rank of a tensor? Key idea: The number of free indices determines the rank (or order) of a tensor. 0 free indices ⇒ rank- 0 tensor (a scalar ); 1 free index ⇒ rank- 1 tensor (a vector ); 2 free indices ⇒ rank- 2 tensor (a matrix ); . . . Important remark This is only an intuition . Later we will see that an object must satisfy additional transformation properties to genuinely qualify as a tensor. So this should not be taken as a formal de˝nition of rank. 6 37

# Page 10^page=10
Vector differential opera- tors

# Page 11^page=11
Scalar and vector fields De˝nition A scalar ˝eld is a map that assigns a real number to every point in space. ϕ : Rn → R A vector ˝eld is a map that assigns a vector to every point in space. ψ : Rn → Rn 7 37

# Page 12^page=12
Differential Operators Di˙erential Operators We will consider three di˙erential operators: The gradient The divergence The curl Each can be expressed in su˚x notation to give more compact formulations and easier calculations. To do this we re-label the Cartesian coordinate system (x, y, z) as (x1, x2, x3). 8 37

# Page 13^page=13
The Gradient De˝nition. The gradient of a scalar ˝eld is ∇f = ( ∂f ∂x1 , ∂f ∂x2 , ∂f ∂x3 ) . Remark. The i-th component of the gradient is the partial derivative with respect to xi. So in su˚x notation we can simply write [∇f ]i = ∂f ∂xi . The gradient of a scalar has one free index i, indicating the result is a vector quantity . 9 37

# Page 14^page=14
The Divergence De˝nition. The divergence of a vector ˝eld u is ∇ · u = ∂u1 ∂x1 + ∂u2 ∂x2 + ∂u3 ∂x3 = ∂uj ∂xj = ∇iui, Remark. There is a dummy index j indicating the summation over j = 1, 2, 3. No free indices indicates the divergence of a vector is a scalar quantity . 10 37

# Page 15^page=15
The Curl De˝nition. The curl of a vector ˝eld u is ∇ × u = ∣ ∣ ∣ ∣ ∣ ∣ i j k ∂ ∂x1 ∂ ∂x2 ∂ ∂x3 u1 u2 u3 ∣ ∣ ∣ ∣ ∣ ∣ = ( ∂u3 ∂x2 − ∂u2 ∂x3 , ∂u1 ∂x3 − ∂u3 ∂x1 , ∂u2 ∂x1 − ∂u1 ∂x2 ) 11 37

# Page 16^page=16
Reminder: Cross product and alternating tensor Because the curl uses the cross product , we can write it using the alternating tensor. Reminder: alternating tensor The alternating tensor ϵijk is de˝ned by ϵijk =    0 if any of i, j, k are equal , +1 if (i, j, k) = (1, 2, 3), (2, 3, 1) or (3, 1, 2), −1 if (i, j, k) = (1, 3, 2), (2, 1, 3) or (3, 2, 1). Reminder: Alternating tensor and cross product Recall that (u × v)i = ϵijkujvk. 12 37

# Page 17^page=17
Curl and cross product Curl and cross product The components of the curl are then [∇ × u]i = ϵijk∇juk = ϵijk ∂uk ∂xj . Remark. The dummy indices j and k indicate a double sum. The free index i indicates the curl of a vector is a vector quantity . 13 37

# Page 18^page=18
Example: The Curl Example: The Curl Let us ˝nd the curl of A = 1 2 x3 1x2i + (4x1x5 2 + 1)j + x2x3 3k at the point Q = (2, 1, 2). ∇ × A = [ ∂ ∂x2 (x2x3 3) − ∂ ∂x3 (4x1x5 2 + 1)] i − [ ∂ ∂x1 (x2x3 3) − ∂ ∂x3 ( 1 2 x3 1x2 )] j + [ ∂ ∂x1 (4x1x5 2 + 1) − ∂ ∂x2 ( 1 2 x 3 1x2 )] k = x3 3i + 0j + (4x5 2 − 1 2 x3 1 ) k. 14 37

# Page 19^page=19
Example: The Curl - Part 2 Example: The Curl Thus, at Q = (2, 1, 2) we have ∇ × A|(2,1,2) = [x3 3i + 0j + ( 4x5 2 − 1 2 x3 1 ) k] (2,1,2) = 8i + 0j + 0k = (8, 0, 0). 15 37

# Page 20^page=20
Vector differential opera- tors

# Page 21^page=21
Position vector De˝nition. The position vector is r = (x1, x2, x3). We denote its magnitude by r = |r|. Next, let us ˝nd the gradient ∇r, the divergence ∇ · r, and the curl ∇ × r of the position vector. 16 37

# Page 22^page=22
Position vector derivatives and the delta Kronecker Position vector derivatives and the delta Kronecker Notice that ∂x1 ∂x1 = 1 but ∂x1 ∂x2 = 0. In general, we have ∂xi ∂xj = { 1 if i = j 0 if i ̸= j = δij. 17 37

# Page 23^page=23
Gradient of vector position The gradient ∇r Let r be the position vector r = (x1, x2, x3) and r = |r|. We ˝rst write r = |r| = (r · r) 1/2 = (xjxj) 1/2. Then we use this to calculate ∇r [∇r]i = ∂ ∂xi (xjxj) 1/2 = 1 2 (xjxj) −1/2 ∂ ∂xi (xjxj) = 1 2r ∂ ∂xi (xjxj) (chain rule) = 1 2r 2xj ∂xj ∂xi (product rule) = 1 r xjδij = xi r = [ r r ] i . 18 37

# Page 24^page=24
Divergence of vector position The divergence ∇ · r Let r be the position vector r = (x1, x2, x3). Let us ˝nd the divergence using su˚x notation ∇ · r = ∂ri ∂xi = ∂xi ∂xi = δii = 3. 19 37

# Page 25^page=25
Curl of vector position The curl ∇ × r Let r be the position vector r = (x1, x2, x3) Let us ˝nd the curl [∇ × r]i = ϵijk ∂xk ∂xj = ϵijkδjk = (0)i, where 0 = (0, 0, 0). In fact, ϵijkδjk = 0 because If j ̸= k, then δjk = 0. If j = k, then ϵijk = 0. This means that ∇ × r = (0, 0, 0). 20 37

# Page 26^page=26
Combinations of grad, div and curl

# Page 27^page=27
Combining Differential Operators Combining Di˙erential Operators We will consider the following combinations of the di˙erential operators 1. Div grad, 2. Curl grad, 3. Grad div, 4. Div curl, 5. Curl curl. We will use su˚x notation because it is much quicker than writing out all the components. 21 37

# Page 28^page=28
Div grad Div grad We will ˝rst compute the combination div grad . But ˝rst, note that this is well de˝ned because grad : scalar ˝eld → vector ˝eld , div : vector ˝eld → scalar ˝eld . Hence div ◦ grad : scalar ˝eld grad −−−→ vector ˝eld div −−→ scalar ˝eld . In other words, div grad is an operator of the form scalar ˝eld → scalar ˝eld . 22 37

# Page 29^page=29
Div grad  Part 2 Div grad Consider scalar ˝eld f . The div grad of f is ∇ · (∇f ) = ∂ ∂xj ([∇f ]j) = ∂ ∂xj ( ∂f ∂xj ) = ∂2f ∂xj∂xj = ∇2f. The symbol ∇2 is known as the Laplacian operator . 23 37

# Page 30^page=30
Curl grad Curl grad Let us compute curl grad . Consider scalar ˝eld f . We have [∇ × (∇f )]i = ϵijk ∂ ∂xj ∂f ∂xk ((w × v)i = ϵijkwjvk) = ϵikj ∂ ∂xk ∂f ∂xj (relabelling j ↔ k) = −ϵijk ∂ ∂xk ∂f ∂xj (ϵikj = −ϵijk) = −ϵijk ∂ ∂xj ∂f ∂xk (order of derivatives does not matter ). 24 37

# Page 31^page=31
Curl grad - remark Curl grad Let us compute curl grad . Consider scalar ˝eld f . We have [∇ × (∇f )]i = grayϵijk ∂ ∂xj ∂f ∂xk ((w × v)i = ϵijkwjvk) = ϵikj ∂ ∂xk ∂f ∂xj (relabelling j ↔ k) = −ϵijk ∂ ∂xk ∂f ∂xj (ϵikj = −ϵijk) = gray−ϵijk ∂ ∂xj ∂f ∂xk (order of derivatives does not matter ). 25 37

# Page 32^page=32
Curl grad - conclusion Curl grad Because [∇ × (∇f )]i = ϵijk ∂ ∂xj ∂f ∂xk = −ϵijk ∂ ∂xj ∂f ∂xk , we conclude [∇ × (∇f )]i = (0)i, that is ∇ × (∇f ) = 0 = (0, 0, 0). 26 37

# Page 33^page=33
Grad div Grad div Let us compute grad div . Consider vector ˝eld u. We have [∇(∇ · u)]i = ∂ ∂xi ( ∂uj ∂xj ) = ∂2uj ∂xi∂xj . This quantity cannot be simpli˝ed any further. 27 37

# Page 34^page=34
Div curl - remark Div curl Let us compute div curl . Consider a vector ˝eld u. We have ∇ · (∇ × u) = ∇i (∇ × u)i (w · v = wivi) = ∇i ( ϵijk ∂uk ∂xj ) ((w × v)i = ϵijkwjvk) = ϵijk ∂ ∂xi ∂uk ∂xj ( ∇i = ∂ ∂xi ) = ϵjik ∂ ∂xj ∂uk ∂xi (relabelling i ↔ j) = −ϵijk ∂ ∂xj ∂uk ∂xi (ϵjik = −ϵijk) = −ϵijk ∂ ∂xi ∂uk ∂xj . (order of derivatives does not matter ) 28 37

# Page 35^page=35
Div curl - conclusion Div curl Let us compute div curl . Consider a vector ˝eld u. We have ∇ · (∇ × u) = ∇i (∇ × u)i (w · v = wivi) = ∇i ( ϵijk ∂uk ∂xj ) ((w × v)i = ϵijkwjvk) = grayϵijk ∂ ∂xi ∂uk ∂xj ( ∇i = ∂ ∂xi ) = ϵjik ∂ ∂xj ∂uk ∂xi (relabelling i ↔ j) = −ϵijk ∂ ∂xj ∂uk ∂xi (ϵjik = −ϵijk) = gray−ϵijk ∂ ∂xi ∂uk ∂xj . (order of derivatives does not matter ) 29 37

# Page 36^page=36
Curl grad-conclusion Curl grad Because ∇ · (∇ × u) = ϵijk ∂ ∂xi ∂uk ∂xj = −ϵijk ∂ ∂xi ∂uk ∂xj , we conclude ∇ · (∇ × u) = 0. 30 37

# Page 37^page=37
Curl curl Curl curl Let us compute curl curl . Consider vector ˝eld u. We have [∇ × (∇ × u)]i = ϵijk ∂ ∂xj (∇ × u)k ((w × v)i = ϵijkwjvk) = ϵijk ∂ ∂xj ϵkℓm ∂um ∂xℓ = ϵijkϵkℓm ∂2um ∂xj∂xℓ = (δiℓδjm − δimδjℓ) ∂2um ∂xj∂xℓ = ∂2uj ∂xj∂xi − ∂2ui ∂xj∂xj = [∇(∇ · u) − ∇2u]i. 31 37

# Page 38^page=38
Curl curl & the Laplacian curl curl & the Laplacian We have shown [∇ × (∇ × u)]i = [∇(∇ · u) − ∇2u]i. That is, ∇ × (∇ × u) = ∇(∇ · u) − ∇2u. This gives us a new description of the vector Laplacian operator. ∇2u = ∇(∇ · u) − ∇ × (∇ × u). 32 37

# Page 39^page=39
Example Example We now use the new description of the Laplacian ∇2u = ∇(∇ · u) − ∇ × (∇ × u), to show that ∇ × (∇2u) = ∇2(∇ × u). First substitute in the identity: ∇ × (∇2u) = ∇ × (∇(∇ · u) − ∇ × (∇ × u)). 33 37

# Page 40^page=40
Example - Part 2 Example Next, we show that ∇ × (∇2u) = ∇2(∇ × u). Using properties of combinations, we get ∇ × (∇2u) = ∇ × (∇(∇ · u) − ∇ × (∇ × u) ) = −∇ × (∇ × (∇ × u)) (since curl grad is zero ) We know that curl curl is ∇ × (∇ × u) = ∇(∇ · u) − ∇2u. Substituting this in the formula above, we get −∇(∇ · (∇ × u)) + ∇2(∇ × u) = ∇2(∇ × u) (div curl is zero ). 34 37

# Page 41^page=41
Example - Part 3 Remark Notice that we have shown ∇ × (∇2u) = ∇2(∇ × u). That is, the operators ∇2 and ∇× commute. 35 37

# Page 42^page=42
Summary: Combinations of grad, div, curl Summary: Combinations of grad, div, curl 1. Div Grad: ∇ · (∇f ) = ∂2f ∂xj∂xj = ∇2f, 2. Curl Grad: ∇ × (∇f ) = 0, 3. Grad Div: [∇(∇ · u)]i = ∂2uj ∂xi∂xj , 4. Div Curl: ∇ · (∇ × u) = 0, 5. Curl Curl: ∇2u = ∇(∇ · u) − ∇ × (∇ × u). 36 37
